items.summary: An extended demo of the action role-playing game

News GAMES The Ultimate Night City mod pack unlocks the full potential of path tracing and DLSS 5 in Cyberpunk 2077 Evgen Kovalov GAMES 20 September 2026 Views: 2735 An extended demo of the action role-playing game's gameplay has been released online. Cyberpunk 2077 With deep graphical modifications, third-person view support, and experimental NVIDIA DLSS 5 neural network rendering in 2X Pass mode. The run was performed on the flagship NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 GPU, whose computing power allowed for the processing of scenes with photorealistic detail. On character models, neural rendering technology provided unprecedented rendering of skin microrelief, pores, moles, expression lines, tattoos, and subcutaneous cybernetic implants. The characters' clothing, including leather vests, thick denim tops, military cargo pants, and textured zippered jackets, features an ES benchmark fiber weave structure without jagged artifacts or pixel noise.

The visual component is based on an updated fan-made Ultimate Night City build, optimized specifically for the DLSS 5 pipeline. The modification includes a custom LUT color correction palette, a reworked ENV weather system, and improved path tracing based on the mod. Ultra Plus, as well as the Reshade add-ons and the RenoDX HDR profile. These graphical enhancements ensured a soft diffusion of benchmark daylight, deep shadows in alleyways, and physically accurate reflections in the mirrors of parked vintage cars, puddles on cracked asphalt, and neon motel signs. At the same time, the developers managed to preserve the authentic, dark style of Night City, eliminating excessively acidic lighting and posterized shadows.

The key gameplay innovation of the build is a fully playable third-person camera modification, currently in active development. The mod features an adaptive switching mechanism that automatically reverts to the default first-person view during dynamic shootouts and cinematic scenes to preserve accurate aiming and dialogue direction. The flagship GeForce RTX 5090 graphics card handled the double workload of the DLSS 5 2X Pass algorithm, maintaining a stable frame rate and smooth character animations as they walk through detailed city blocks without ghosting or blurring.

items.title: How CD PROJEKT RED Built the Immersive World of Cyberpunk 2077
items.summary: CD PROJEKT RED’s art directors explain how Night City was handcrafted, how first-person gameplay shaped its scale and detail, why path tracing fit its lighting pipeline, and what Phantom Liberty changed.
items.content:
CD PROJEKT RED’s art directors explain how Night City was handcrafted, how first-person gameplay shaped its scale and detail, why path tracing fit its lighting pipeline, and what Phantom Liberty changed.

Cyberpunk 2077 Has Reached 40 Million Copies Sold

Few video game settings are as immediately recognizable as Cyberpunk 2077’s Night City. Its towering corporate architecture, overcrowded streets, omnipresent advertising, and densely layered districts create the impression of a metropolis that existed long before the player arrived. According to CD PROJEKT RED, that effect was achieved almost entirely by hand: artists placed everything from buildings and advertisements to trash containers and individual sheets of paper, using procedural tools only as starting points in a limited number of cases.

In this interview, VP and Global Art Director Jakub Knapik and Environment Art Director Kacper Niepokólczycki explain the artistic and technical thinking behind that world. They break down Night City’s four chronological visual styles, the “rule of contrast” used to keep its districts distinctive, and the challenge of creating controlled chaos without overwhelming the player. The pair also discuss why Cyberpunk 2077 required twice the texel density of The Witcher 3 , how its first-person perspective transformed environmental composition, and why the studio’s physically grounded lighting pipeline made path tracing feel like a natural evolution rather than a complete reinvention.

Knapik and Niepokólczycki describe how clearer visual guidelines helped Phantom Liberty become more detailed but less noisy, while multidisciplinary teams improved communication between art, design, narrative, and gameplay. That structural change ultimately made the expansion one of the smoothest development experiences the studio’s art leaders had encountered, and provided lessons that will continue to inform CD Projekt Red’s future projects.

Cyberpunk 2077 has had an extraordinary journey since its release and has continued to evolve for years. Looking back at the game today, what are you most proud of about what the team ultimately created?

Kacper Niepokólczycki, Environment Art Director: Great question. For me personally… A lot; the whole game, if I might be honest. Moving into a whole new IP, with new features like the first-person perspective, was a huge learning process for us, and at the same time we were building new technology from scratch. I’m proud of the team on every single front, and I’m not talking about only the development team. I’m talking about every single person working in our studio — devs, back office, IT... Every single person was a huge part of the success of Cyberpunk 2077.

Going into specifics, I'm super proud of Night City and the Badlands, how the game looks and feels, and how original Night City is. The whole Art team, but also a lot of other teams, collaborated to create an incredible experience of exploration, really breathing and living in Night City. I’m still hypnotized when I watch all those YouTube videos of people walking or driving through Night City or the Badlands and just taking it all in — the atmosphere, vibes, and density. That's what I call immersion, and I think we did create an incredibly immersive world.

Night City is such a huge part of the Cyberpunk franchise and I’m proud we were able to make it feel so authentic. Even looking at Edgerunners, it takes place in this exact same, tangible world.

Jakub Knapik, VP, Global Art Director: I second every word from Kacper. At the same time, in retrospect, I wanted to bring up one element that, to me, makes Cyberpunk very memorable. From the day I joined the project, I sensed that overwhelming feeling of working on something truly special. Some could say we all say that in retrospect. Fair. But that feeling of the project being special or different was lifted to the artistic level; it was a mindset. And I believe it was so powerful and present in our minds that it actually shifted the philosophy, or the decision-making, of how this game was made.

We tried to make a believable world, one that would not just be a background for gameplay, but could be almost a sandbox for an alternate life in this Cyberpunk world. That paradigm was present in Art, in the way we created multilayered styles in the city and its history, the way characters are created and designed, and in the way we created very ambitious cinematics without cuts — decisions which led to the quests and gameplay itself. In all these moments, we tried to avoid the most obvious decisions and find our own unique approach and a coherent feel for the game. That's why I believe our players so often like to go back to Night City and just hang out. Ride in a car, listen to music, do a side quest, buy an apartment, and just breathe the air of this world.

That is also why Cyberpunk 2077 is so unmistakably Cyberpunk 2077. I am super proud of the depth of the experience and its brave uniqueness, created by our team.

What were the core visual pillars established for Night City, and which rules did environment and concept artists use to make sure every district felt different while still belonging to the same city? Jakub Knapik: Cyberpunk is all about contrast — the contrast of familiarity and social fear reflected in the mirror of technology, in the creation of some sort of dystopian vision. To create familiarity, we again used rules we know from the real world. When we walk down the street, we see multiple layers of time, creating some sort of visual storytelling about the place and the people. We read that complex encoding subconsciously. And it often tells us more about the place than words describing it. No city has just one period, one architectural style, or people dressing in one kind of clothing. All of these details tell a story about society and provide relatable context. So when crafting Night City, we looked at all the visual concepts and visual tributes we created during the preproduction phase, and tried to encode their styles into time layers that would create Night City's history. As a trio, we spent over a week on an Art Directors' offsite, where, together with the Environment Art Director Lucjan Więcek and Character Art Director Paweł Mielniczuk, we created a simple backstory of the city's progression and organized the styles into a proper chronology.

That is how we created a bleached, 80s-inspired entropy — our take on retro Cyberpunk . Newer in Night City is an almost naive, 60s-inspired, vibrant, yet very plasticky kitsch style that brought energy and a much-needed layer of color to the precious era. Then came the very corporate, intimidating, power-projecting, and utilitarian neomilitarism, which we used to highlight very modern designs and the omnipresence of corporations in the city. And finally, the super rare, fake, and pseudo-natural shape-driven neo-kitsch — a style that allows the ultra-rich to pretend they care about the world and nature. Those were the synonyms, encoded visual patterns, and connotations that we used as a vocabulary. Additionally, every district had its own story, with color coding that best matched its theme. The map was also well thought out and highly functional, with logical layers of time, communities, the most active corporations, and themes told through crafted versions of these styles used as building blocks. That created a very complex, dimensional visual storytelling maze of Night City, one you can hopefully read and understand like you would in every city in the real world.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Comes to Battle.net in 2026
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 comes to Battle.net in 2026. Here’s why another storefront and Blizzard crossovers caught my attention.
items.content:
When I heard Cyberpunk 2077 was coming to Battle.net, my first reaction was, “Oh wait, what? Isn’t Battle.net a Microsoft thing?” I was interested in seeing what the benefits to CD PROJEKT RED were. Is this just another platform for distribution, or is there a deeper collaboration?

Cyberpunk 2077 is CD PROJEKT RED’s open-world RPG set in Night City. I haven’t played more than 10–15 hours of it, but I follow it. I pretty much have a copy of it everywhere, including Steam and GOG.

So, for me particularly, this wouldn’t change too much. I’d much rather play my GOG copy because of its DRM-free access. But I’m interested in what another storefront does for the game.

CD PROJEKT RED announced at BlizzCon 2026 that Cyberpunk 2077 will arrive on Battle.net later this year. Players can buy the base game and Phantom Liberty separately, or get both through the Ultimate Edition. The announcement doesn’t give an exact date or prices.

This gives CD PROJEKT RED exposure to another storefront, but Battle.net makes this particularly interesting. I’ve always associated Battle.net mostly with Blizzard games. You open it to play something like Diablo , Overwatch , or World of Warcraft . So seeing Cyberpunk 2077 sitting alongside those games is going to feel a little strange.

But that also helps answer my original question. For CD PROJEKT RED, Battle.net puts Cyberpunk 2077 in front of another established PC audience. Then you add the Cyberpunk and Witcher crossovers with Blizzard games, and the partnership starts to make more sense than simply putting the game on another storefront.

They’re not redoing the IP. They’re finding another audience for something they already have. I think it’s a good move for them, although I wonder what the price will look like now that the game’s been out for a while.

The partnership also includes Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and Edgerunners 2 collaborations coming to Overwatch in 2027. Alongside that, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered heads to Battle.net on September 29, with Songs of the Past following in 2027.

Diablo IV is getting a Geralt-themed Barbarian skin tied to eligible Battle.net purchases of Songs of the Past . More Witcher content is coming in 2027.

The crossovers didn’t do too much for me personally, but I’m happy for the players they do affect. You’re leaning on the other side to hopefully bring them over to your side. If that audience likes your product, there’s room for them to pick it up. That’s where I see the opportunity.

items.title: As Cyberpunk 2 continues on Unreal, CD Projekt CEO says "REDengine was "not really the issue", they just never wanted to "make technology"
items.summary: CD Projekt Red CEO Michał Nowakowski explains why Cyberpunk 2 is using Unreal Engine 5 after the launch of Cyberpunk 2077.
items.content:
Games Blog News Features Guides Evergreen guides for popular games, written by our in-house experts. FAQs Tutorials As Cyberpunk 2 continues on Unreal, CD Projekt CEO says “REDengine was “not really the issue”, they just never wanted to “make technology” Published:

After the release of Cyberpunk 2077 , CD Projekt Red has moved entirely to Unreal Engine 5 for its suite of upcoming games: The Witcher 4, Cyberpunk 2 , and more. While some have correlated this change with the disastrous launch of the studio’s last release, co-CEO Michał Nowakowski explains that this isn’t necessarily the case.

Right now, The Witcher 4 is deep in development with an expected release date of 2028. Alongside the fantasy RPG, Cyberpunk 2 is currently in early development with over a hundred developers working on the game. (It’s also more-than-likely following the first-person cutscene direction of the first game !)

In an interview with Deconstructor of Fun , Nowakowski explained that Cyberpunk’s release was part of the push towards Unreal Engine 5, but not because the studio’s engine couldn’t support the scale of RPGs it wanted to make.

“Yes and no,” the CEO said. “A lot of people think like this, but this is a bit of a false assumption, I would say, because the issue with Cyberpunk was not really REDengine itself.” Instead, the issues stemmed from the fact that CD Projekt Red was not set up to support an engine of that scope in the way they needed to.

“The dream of the company was actually never to make technology,” the CEO continued. “It was to, yes, create visually and technically cutting-edge games, but most importantly, telling the stories in the most convincing and immersive way.”

“We feel we’re going to be able to tell more stories and launch more games, because we’re not going to be responsible for creating the technology from scratch.”

Nowakowski revealed that Epic Games’ Unreal Engine 5 tech demo of The Matrix Awakens, a realistically-rendered open-world city set within the iconic sci-fi world, is what convinced the team to make the engine switch, not the state of Cyberpunk 2077.

“It was not the Cyberpunk launch that convinced us to abandon the REDengine and switch completely to to Unreal Engine 5 with the future projects. It was more the moment we got an early scoop of the Matrix demo that Epic made. We then asked ourselves: ‘Is UE5 ready to ship a game like we make?’”

The CD Projekt CEO explained that the engine simply wasn’t ready for what they wanted to do. However, the company decided to push for a “strategic collaboration” with Epic to improve the engine and make it more efficient for the types of games that CDPR makes.

“We’re actually, I think, the only team in the world outside of Epic that deals with the inside of the ‘black box’ that the engine is. Nobody else is doing that except for us and them, which we do through collaborative efforts together.

“And by doing so, we feel we’re going to be able to tell more stories and launch more games, because we’re not going to be responsible for creating the technology from scratch, but rather creating for that technology little things that actually make a big difference for the specific kinds of games that we make.”

It’s going to be a long time until we get to see any of Cyberpunk 2, but CD Projekt Red’s first Unreal Engine 5 game will be The Witcher 4. Right now, the game is still in development, but we’ve already seen an impressive tech demo for the game running on a base PS5, and it looks leagues above the rendering capabilities of its predecessor.

Lewis White is a veteran games journalist with over a decade in the field. Starting with beloved Xbox website ICXM/XboxMAD, Lewis became the Gaming Editor at MSPoweruser before becoming the Editor in Chief of StealthOptional and Gfinityesports. Lewis later jumped to By Gamers For Gamers where he jumped to become EIC of VideoGamer and the host of the New VideoGamer Podcast prior to the website’s acquisition.

items.content:
Xbox Game Pass is shaking up its library in a few weeks and a major CD Projekt RED title will be rotating off of the service.

Cyberpunk 2077 join Xbox Game Pass earlier this year in March 2026. The CD Projekt RED title has made major improvements and updates since its rocky launch back in 2020 and has become a must-play RPG for many fans of the genre.

Unfortunately, the lengthy open-world game won’t be sticking around the Xbox Game Pass library much longer. Along with the announcement of all the games coming to Xbox Game Pass in the first half of September, Xbox also revealed a long list of titles that are rotating off of the service.

Amongst the list of games leaving on September 15 was Cyberpunk 2077 .

Cyberpunk 2077 is a pretty length game, but it’s definitely possible for subscribers to jump in and play through a lot of the story before September 15 arrives. The average playtime for the main story along is around 25-30 hours. Players who want to dive into all the side missions will likely spend closer to 50 hours in the game.

Although there are some exciting titles arriving in the early weeks of September, Xbox Game Pass is also taking a big hit with the removal of ten titles. In addition to Cyberpunk 2077, gamers may also miss Deep Rock Galactic Survivor and Dead Cells , in particular.

Here is the full list of every time rotating out of the Xbox Game Pass library when September 15 arrives.

As always, players who want to keep any of these titles should consider checking the Xbox store for special deals and discounts before they rotate off of the Xbox Game Pass library. There should be decent savings available while the games are still officially a part of Game Pass, as long as shoppers are subscribers.

Be sure to check back soon for more CD Projekt RED news and other updates on the Xbox Game Pass lineup.

Cyberpunk 2077 is available now on PC, PS5, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox consoles.

Cyberpunk 2077 Is Leaving Xbox Game Pass This Month
items.summary: Play it while you can, choom
items.content:
By Willa Rowe Published Sep 1, 2026, 2:49 PM EDT Willa Rowe is a contributing writer at Polygon, covering games and entertainment. She is a New York-based journalist and critic whose work has been featured in Kotaku, Digital Trends, the A.V. Club, GamesRadar+, and more. She also co-hosts the Girl Mode podcast. News Play it while you can, choom

Image: CD Projekt Red Cyberpunk 2077 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Xbox has announced the latest batch of removals from Game Pass . On Sept. 15, 10 games will leave the service. The biggest name on the list is Cyberpunk 2077 ; CD Projekt Red's once floundering and now flourishing sci-fi RPG.

Cyberpunk 2077 was added in March, so it will have been on the service for only six months. Just last month, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was also removed from Game Pass, perhaps to incentivize players to purchase the upcoming remaster on Sept. 29. As for Cyberpunk 2077 , the sequel is a long way off, but a second season of the acclaimed Edgerunners anime is set to be released on Oct. 20 exclusively on Netflix. That will likely boost interest in the game, which CD Projekt Red will want to capitalize on.

There are nine other games leaving Game Pass on Sept. 15 alongside Cyberpunk 2077. Here's the full list:

Image: Thunder Lotus Games The roguelike Metroidvania Dead Cells is another big loss for the service. The 2018 title remains one of the best entries in the popular genre. Fans of Dead Cells will want to keep an eye on developer Evil Empire's next title, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse , which will be released on Oct. 15. Spiritfarer , a deeply emotional indie about ferrying the recently deceased to the afterlife, is also worth experiencing before it leaves the service.

As for additions, Game Pass is only getting seven new titles. Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War joins the service on Sept. 8. The other additions are Shelldiver, Speedrunners 2: King of Speed, The Royal Writ, Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage, and RuneScape: Dragonwilds .

items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

items.content:
Surviving the City of Dreams is tough, but a choom at your side can make all the difference.

In our latest It’s All About You episode, we’re celebrating all of our iconic duos living on the edge! Night City wouldn’t shine quite so bright without them. 

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners in the most creative ways possible. Don't forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY. See you in the next episode!

items.title: Update 2.3 Patch Notes

items.content:
Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as support for AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, Intel XeSS 2.0 and HDR10+ Gaming, among others.

Update 2.3 also brings Cyberpunk 2077 to a whole new platform: Mac with Apple silicon! If you already own the game on Steam, you can play it on your compatible device. To find out whether your Mac can run Cyberpunk 2077, please check the official requirements.

Read the list of changes for more info:

Vehicles

  • Added 4 new vehicles, including several Side Jobs tied to acquiring them:

    • Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Hunt and The Beast In Me).

      An additional side job unlocks the CrystalCoat™ feature for it.

      [/*]

    • Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred"

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Beast in Me: Badlands, The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo, Transmission, and Search and Destroy)."

      [/*]

    • Yaiba ASM-R250 Muramasa

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, purchase 1 Yaiba vehicle, purchase at least 3 vehicles through AUTOFIXER, and complete Reported Crime: You Play with Fire...).

      If you fail the side job, the vehicle can later be purchased through AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]

    • Chevillon Legatus 450 Aquila

      Available for purchase on AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Introducing AutoDrive! This cutting-edge, autonomous driving feature will take you to your chosen destination (i.e. job objective or placed pin on the map). If you have no set destination, it will take you on a leisurely ride through the streets of Night City. Simply hop in any of your vehicles, make sure you're on a road, and hold G (PC) / Left Stick (consoles) to activate. This feature is disabled when you enter combat or when your vehicle is heavily damaged.

    [/*]

  • Implemented Cinematic Camera for AutoDrive. Hold Q (PC) / D-Pad Right (consoles) to activate. Sit back and enjoy cinematic views of Night City as you cruise toward your destination.

    [/*]

  • Self-driving Delamain cabs are now available on demand! Simply open the menu to call vehicles, then select "Delamain Cab" from the list to request a ride. This feature unlocks after completing the job Don't Lose Your Mind (regardless of outcome) and receiving a message from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ is now available for vehicles from partner brands, including motorcycles. Additionally, the infamous hacker known as Cosmetic_Troll exploited a vulnerability and created a cracked version of Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ technology for lower-end vehicles. Please note, however, that some models do not support the technology, such as heavily modded nomad vehicles and job-related vehicles.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color schemes did not work properly on the Mizutani Shion MZ1 and MZ2.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color scheme could not be applied properly to the Villefort Deleon "Vindicator".

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Added 27 new NPCs that can be spawned in Photo Mode, including Rita Wheeler, the Cassel twins, fixers, Dum Dum, the iguana, Brendan, and more.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between alternative outfits for NPCs spawned in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between V's saved Wardrobe outfits in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Added a confirmation pop-up when exiting Photo Mode to prevent accidental exits after setting up the perfect shot.

    [/*]

  • Added more customization options to the Look-At Camera feature, including an option for only the character's eyes to turn toward the camera instead of their entire body.

    [/*]

  • Added improvements to Lighting:

    • Lights now spawn around the camera instead of the player character.

      [/*]

    • Added an outline to the spotlight mesh and an indicator when it's off screen for better visibility.

      [/*]

    • Improved light movement speed on controllers.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Added multiple new stickers and frames, including iconic quotes and stylish overlays that let you turn your screenshots into Night City postcards – perfect for sharing memories from the City of Dreams.

    [/*]

  • Improved Depth of Field and moved it to the Camera tab.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Color Balance tab, allowing you to create your own custom filters.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Time and Weather tab:

    • Weather: includes rain, acid rain, fog, sandstorm, pollution, and sunny.

      [/*]

    • Time of Day: changes the time of day within Photo Mode.

      [/*]

    • Frame Forward: advances through an unlimited amount of frames to capture the perfect shot.

      [/*]

    • Game Speed: allows in-game time to progress while in Photo Mode."

      [/*]
    [/*]

Quality of Life & Accessibility

  • The game will now detect if the player is using inverted mouse button settings and automatically adjusts in-game button prompts accordingly.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to toggle aiming down sights in Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Jobs & Open World

  • Cyberpsycho Sighting: Bloody Ritual - the "Crack the ritualist's shard" objective now properly disappears from the Journal after completing the objective.

    [/*]

  • Sex on Wheels - now properly appears in the Journal after receiving the message from Jake Estevez.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where selecting a specific dialogue option in the conversation with Bree created a nameless, iconless item in the player's Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where the button to go to the lower level didn't appear on the elevator panel.

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where, when using a controller in Trauma Drama, the controllable character would default to shooting upwards instead of forward.

    [/*]

  • Players can now drop more Cyberware Capacity Shards if some within the intended drop limit were previously missed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing automatic weapons to fire slower than intended.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Official BARGHEST Tac Vest didn't drop from the scripted Airdrop as intended.

    [/*]

  • The level 60 Engineer perk no longer activates the EMP blast outside of combat or after entering a vehicle.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to replay the gameplay tutorial at any time via Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Added an option to tell Johnny to go away after you look at him for a short while when he appears in the passenger seat. He takes the hint and disappears as a passenger for a couple days.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the sound of V's Radioport could be randomly interrupted by the Radioports of nearby NPCs.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where History by Gazelle Twin and Trash Generation played too loudly compared to other songs on the radio.

    [/*]

  • Improved the HDR Setting screen: fixed the HDR calibration preview so it correctly reflects the chosen settings, and clarified the description of the "Tone-Mapping Midpoint" setting.

    [/*]

  • Updated the End User Licence Agreement. You will be asked to accept it again when you load the game after updating.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several visual issues with missing, clipping, or floating textures.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several localization issues in various languages.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 for compatible AMD GPUs. IMPORTANT: The FSR 4 option will not be available in the in-game settings until the supporting AMD driver is installed. Please note that the driver will be released at a later date.

    [/*]

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution Frame Generation 3.1 for compatible hardware. It can now be used in combination with any upscaler.

    [/*]

  • Added support for ​Intel XeSS 2.0, with XeSS Frame Generation available on compatible hardware.

    [/*]

  • Added support for HDR10+ GAMING certified Intel GPUs. To enable this feature, your display must support the technology (find my display) and have "Game Mode" enabled. The HDR10+ GAMING toggle can be found in Settings in the Video tab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the DLSS Super Resolution Preset would invisibly revert from the CNN model to the Transformer model after restarting the game, even though the UI still displayed the CNN model as active.

    [/*]

  • Added more detailed information to the DLSS Super Resolution Preset tooltip in Settings to help players choose the best option for their setup.

    [/*]

  • Added the ability to move the mouse cursor to a different display while in Windowed Borderless mode.

    [/*]

  • Increased the maximum save size from 12 MB to 15 MB.

    [/*]

  • It will now be possible to rebind the key used to jump out of vehicles with the Stuntjock perk.

    [/*]
